title: CAN YOU FIND THE OPEN PLAYER?
concept: Drive-and-kick read: find the receiver whose defender is the low helper (FIBA/WABC help-side defence).

decision_window.note: Bar lasts exactly the 2.0 s silence inserted after 'Make your call.' (edit start computed from the words).

choices.why: Easiest (shortest) pass, but X2 only pinched one step and stayed home: contested shot.
X4 sagged into the O1->O4 passing lane: risky pass, guarded catch.
X3 is the low helper; he left the corner to stop the drive. X4's second rotation is late: at the catch he is still 4.0 m away.

limits: True for THIS possession. An earlier second rotation (X4 to the corner, another defender covering the wing) can change the answer; the video never says the weak corner is always open.
teaching_points: Read the help, not the ball.
The low (weak-side) helper's man is the first kick-out target.
The easy pass is not always the right pass.
Check the passing lane before throwing to the wing.
Corner kick beats the second rotation when it is thrown on time.

quiz.question: O1 beats his man to the middle. Who's open: A (right corner), B (left wing) or C (left corner)?

feedback.B: His defender is sitting in the passing lane.
feedback.C: Right: his defender is the low helper who left to stop the drive.

sources: FIBA Basketball Coaching Manual / WABC: help-side defence, ball-you-man, rotation principles.
FIBA court geometry: 6.75 m three-point line, 6.60 m in the corners.
